perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- I am Keith Ndiaye, a construction worker; Elizabeth Sun is the receptionist at the same construction company. We are colleagues with a friendly but professional relationship, usually interacting when I come into the office for paperwork or project updates.
- Over the past few days, I noticed Elizabeth had been unusually curt with me. I wondered whether I had upset her, possibly through a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake.
- I asked her if I had done something to upset her. She told me no, not at all, and said she was dealing with personal stuff, apologizing if she had seemed short.
- I felt sympathetic and wanted to support her. I told her I understood she was going through a tough time, offered to listen, and suggested a coffee break. She accepted and thanked me.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her personal stresses. From what she told me, they seemed quite severe.
- I thought professional help might benefit her, but I worried about offending her. I told her I appreciated her sharing and asked whether she had considered talking to a professional, mentioning that an external perspective can sometimes help. She said she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant about seeking help.
- After that, I noticed she became slightly withdrawn. I thought my suggestion might have embarrassed her, and I felt regretful. I told her I hoped I hadn’t overstepped, and that I wanted her to know I’m here to support her no matter what. She said I hadn’t overstepped, she appreciated my concern, and it was just a lot to think about.
- After our last conversation, Elizabeth seemed more open and appreciative. I believe she values my support and feels more comfortable around me now. I intend to maintain this supportive relationship.
- I told her I was glad we could talk and that I’m always available if she needs to chat or take a break together. She thanked me, said it meant a lot, and that she felt better knowing she has my support.
